say: I don't like to complain, dear. But the stands were awful cold for the little ones.
My knees and I have had a hard week in this building.
@how_are_things

options.text: I'm sorry. What would make it better?
It's an old building. Bear with us.
Rinks are hard. Take it or leave it.

say: That's my grandchild out there! At {event}! The one in the red. No, the other red.
I knitted a toque for the occasion. It has a pom-pom. For luck.
{event}! Isn't it wonderful? I'll cry. I always cry.

options.text: Which one's yours?
They're lucky to have you here.

say: Good morning, dear. I always come early. I like a good seat and a good chat.
Oh, it's early. I've been up since five. I do that now.

options.text: Good to see you anyway.

say: Hello, sweetheart. I brought lemon squares. One's for you. Two, if nobody's looking.
There's my favourite owner. You look tired. Are you eating?

options.text: Good to see you too, {known_as}.

say: @how_are_things
Hello, dear. What can I do for you?
Oh, it's you. Sit with me a moment.

options.text: Tell me about your grandkids.
What brings you to the rink?
What do you make of the rink?
Any news on the bench?
What would make this place better for you?
Take care.

say: My grandson's in minor hockey. His father played here too. Same dressing room. Same drip.
My granddaughter skates figure. She spins so fast I have to look away.
I've got three grandchildren in three different programs. I live here now, I think.

options.text: They sound wonderful.
Tell me a bit about yourself.
Glad you come.
Good to know you, {known_as}.

say: It's a bit cold up in the stands, dear. My blanket is earning its keep.
The roof still drips. When their father played here it dripped too. Lovely, really.
@ice

options.text: The ice has been better lately, hasn't it?
Noticed the work on the building?
Fair enough. We're working on it.

say: The ice looks lovely and smooth. Nobody's taking a nasty spill.
Good ice! The children are skating so nicely. Well done, dear.

options.text: Glad it shows.

say: The stands are warmer now. I only needed one blanket today.
The washrooms are lovely now. I won't say more. But lovely.

options.text: That's the idea.

say: Lisa Cormier bakes muffins before every game. Blueberry. I told her she should sell them.
Lorraine at the Hot Stove makes Earl's gravy and lets him take the credit. Don't tell anyone, dear.

options.text: Ha. Good to know.

say: Warmer stands, dear. A little heat for the grandparents. We're not getting younger.
Some heaters in the stands. Or blankets. I'd knit them if you asked.

options.text: I'll see what I can do.
Can't promise anything, but noted.
You're not the first to say it. It's on the list.

say: Off you go, dear. Mind the ice.
Goodbye, sweetheart. Come see me next game.
